title: Partial-wave decomposition of the $p$--$^{5}_Λ\mathrm{He}$ correlation function: a femtoscopic route to the $^{6}_Λ\mathrm{Li}$ resonance
summary: The hypernucleus $^{6}_Λ\mathrm{Li}$ is unbound against proton emission, so its resonances appear in the low-momentum $p$--$^{5}_Λ\mathrm{He}$ correlation function, which femtoscopy can measure. We compute this correlation function in an $α+Λ$ folding model of $^{5}_Λ\mathrm{He}$: phenomenological $pα$ and $pΛ$ interactions are averaged over the internal $α$--$Λ$ motion, and a single $ΛN$ strength factor is fixed by the measured $^{6}_Λ\mathrm{He}$ binding energy. The model places the $^{6}_Λ\mathrm{Li}$ $1^{-}$ state at $E_{R}=0.60^{+0.11}_{-0.10}$~MeV with $Γ=0.18\pm0.05$~MeV and produces a pronounced peak in $C(k^{*})$ near $31~\mathrm{MeV}/c$. The predicted peak position, $k^{*}_{\rm peak}=\sqrt{2μE_{R}}=30.8\pm2.6~\mathrm{MeV}/c$, is uncertain mainly because of the measured $B_Λ(^{6}_Λ\mathrm{He})$, not because of the $ΛN$ interaction. An exact partial-wave decomposition shows that the $P$ wave accounts for the entire enhancement over the Coulomb baseline, $79\%$ of it from the $1^{-}$ channel. A Lednický--Lyuboshitz analysis restricted to $S$ waves therefore cannot describe this system. The maximum of the $1^{-}$ channel lies within $1\%$ of $k^{*}_{\rm peak}$, but the unresolved $2^{-}$ state and the momentum resolution shift the measured maximum upward by $2.4~\mathrm{MeV}/c$ at $σ_{k^{*}}=3~\mathrm{MeV}/c$.

title: Wigner distribution modeling of nuclear state in NuWro Monte Carlo event generator
summary: We develop a method to use the Wigner distribution (WD) description of the nuclear initial state of $^{12}$C, $^{16}$O, $^{40}$Ar, and $^{56}$Fe for quasielastic scattering in the NuWro Monte Carlo event generator. We propose two different algorithms to deal with the problem of negative values of the WDs. In our treatment, finite-nucleus WDs provide a correlation between the position and the momentum of bound nucleons that is very different from what is assumed in the standard approaches based on the Fermi gas model and spectral functions. We show that the use of WDs leads to effects that can be measured experimentally and may be relevant for future neutrino oscillation experiments.

title: Manifestation of scale symmetry in nuclear medium
comment: Contribution to the volume to be published in Journal of Subatomic Particles and Cosmology in memorial of Prof. Mannque Rho
summary: This memorial tribute to Mannque Rho focuses on the role of scale symmetry in baryonic matter, especially on its profound influence on the possible resolution of the ``quenched $g_A$" problem in the Gamow-Teller transition of nuclei, the pseudoconformal structure of dense nuclear matter and the origin of the peak of sound velocity of nuclear matter. The discussion is based on the genuine dilaton scenario, anchored on the Crewther-Tunstall infrared fixed point, which provides a unified framework where scale symmetry---broken explicitly by the QCD trace anomaly---can be spontaneously broken, yielding the scalar $f_0(500)$ as a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson. In nuclear medium, this scenario serves as a natural foundation of the Brown-Rho scaling---a relation that has been central to nuclear physics for over three decades. The sound velocity of nuclear matter exhibits a characteristic peak at intermediate densities arising from the kink behavior of the dilaton field, a unique signature of scale symmetry realization that distinguishes the dilaton-compensated effective theory from conventional Walecka-type models. At higher densities, the approach to the dilaton-limit fixed point produces pseudo-conformal behavior with sound velocity $v_s^2 = 1/3$ saturating from below at $n \gtrsim 3n_0$, while the trace of the energy-momentum tensor remains nonzero. The framework also provides a natural resolution of the long-standing ``quenched $g_A$" problem, demonstrating that nuclear correlations, not fundamental quenching, account for the effective axial coupling approaching unity. The continuity from the unitary limit at low density to the dilaton limit at high density suggests a pervasive role for scale symmetry in nuclear dynamics across all density regimes.

title: Comparison of Methods for Extracting Three-Dimensional Lévy Source Parameters in $\sqrt{s_{\text{NN}}} = 200\text{ GeV}$ Au+Au Collisions with EPOS3
comment: 17 pages, 4 figures. Presented at the 18th Workshop on Particle Correlations and Femtoscopy, May 18-22, 2026, Budapest, Hungary
summary:
Bose--Einstein femtoscopy probes the spatiotemporal geometry of the particle-emitting source in heavy-ion collisions, where experimental data favor a Lévy-stable source description. We compare four approaches for extracting 3D Lévy source parameters using $π^+π^+$ pairs from EPOS3-simulated Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\text{NN}}} = 200\text{ GeV}$: direct fits to the pair-source distribution $D(\boldsymbolρ)$, and fits to the two-particle correlation function $C(\boldsymbol{q})$ obtained via (i) the CRAB package, (ii) direct numerical integration of $D(\boldsymbolρ)$, and (iii) fast Fourier transformation (FFT). On an identical momentum grid, numerical integration and FFT are analytically identical and numerically equivalent ($\text{RMSE} < 10^{-14}$), while FFT reduces the computation time from hours to seconds.
  We extract the transverse-mass dependence of the Lévy radii, Lévy index $α$, and correlation strength $λ$ in $0\text{--}10\,\%$ central collisions. All methods reproduce the same physical trends, but CRAB results fluctuate due to event pooling, and correlation-function fits deviate systematically from direct source fits, e.g., with $\sim 7\text{--}9\,\%$ lower $α$. These deviations may reflect residual non-Lévy features of the source, probed differently in coordinate and momentum space, and the comparison of event-averaged parameters with fits to the ensemble-accumulated source, a mixture of Lévy distributions with lower effective $α$.

title: Analysis of Xe-131 Prompt Gammas
summary: The prompt gammas of Xe-131 from thermal neutron capture were measured for the first time at the Fission Product Prompt gamma-ray Spectrometer by irradiation of isotopically enriched Xe-130 in a high-purity quartz ampoule. Through gamma-gamma coincidences, 42 new prompt gammas were measured and 14 new nuclear states determined.

title: Linking chiral nuclear forces to light-ion collisions: a global sensitivity analysis
comment: 5 pages, 2 figures, plus 2 pages End Matter with 2 figures and 2 tables
summary: Ultrarelativistic $^{16}$O+$^{16}$O and $^{20}$Ne+$^{20}$Ne collisions recently performed at the Large Hadron Collider have imaged quadrupole and octupole correlations between nucleons through the collective flow of emitted hadrons. We establish a quantitative link between these correlations and the low-energy constants (LECs) that enter chiral inter-nucleon interactions. Emulators built using the subspace-projected coupled-cluster method enable a global sensitivity analysis of the ground-state quadrupole mean-square eccentricity, revealing that quadrupole correlations respond linearly and additively to all 16 LECs at next-to-next-to-leading order in the chiral expansion. The sensitivities differ markedly in $^{16}$O and $^{20}$Ne, and are complementary to those of the binding energy and charge radius, the bulk observables to which nuclear interactions are typically calibrated. In particular, $^{20}$Ne collisions dominantly probe the spin-orbit part of two-nucleon interactions. Soft-particle correlations in light-ion collisions thus constitute a new type of data to study nuclear forces and their emergence from quantum chromodynamics.

title: Exploring the limit of partonic collectivity in small collision systems at the LHC
comment: 21 pages, 4 captioned figures, authors from page 16, submitted to PLB, figures at http://alice-publications.web.cern.ch/node/13697
summary: The existence of a partonic phase in small collision systems has been investigated previously through measurements of the elliptic flow ($v_{2}$) of mesons ($π^{\pm}$, K$^{\pm}$, and K$_{S}^{0}$) and baryons ($\rm{p}(\overline{\rm{p}})$, $Λ(\overlineΛ)$) in high-multiplicity p-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.02$ TeV and pp collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV recorded by ALICE. The results have revealed a grouping and splitting behavior of $v_{2}$ for baryons and mesons at intermediate transverse momentum ($p_{\rm{T}}$), establishing that partonic collectivity, as observed in heavy-ion collisions, is also present in these systems. In this Letter, the $p_{\rm{T}}$-differential $v_{2}$ of various hadronic species is investigated in p-Pb collisions for the multiplicity intervals $N_{\rm ch} \geq 50$, $25 \leq N_{\rm ch} < 50$, and $15 \leq N_{\rm ch} < 25$, as well as in pp collisions for $25 \leq N_{\rm ch} < 50$ and $15 \leq N_{\rm ch} < 25$. Here, $N_{\rm ch}$ is the efficiency-corrected number of charged particles produced in the kinematic region of $|η|< 0.8$ and $0.2 < p_{\rm T} < 3.0$ GeV/$c$. The characteristic mass dependence of $v_{2}$, as well as the grouping and splitting patterns among identified particles, are examined. The results in both p-Pb and pp collisions with $N_{\rm ch} \geq 25$ are consistent with the development of partonic collectivity. In the low-multiplicity region, $15 \leq N_{\rm ch} < 25$, the baryon-to-meson $v_{2}$ splitting, as quantified by the baryon-to-meson $v_2$ ratios, remains broadly consistent with that at higher multiplicities. However, its significance decreases to $\sim2σ$ in p-Pb collisions and to less than $1σ$ in pp collisions owing to the sizable experimental uncertainties. These measurements constitute the first steps towards identifying the limits of partonic flow in small collision systems at the LHC.

title: Chiral invariant mass and scale symmetry in dense matter from a dilaton compensated parity doublet model
summary: In the parity doublet model the nucleon mass includes a chiral invariant part $m_0$, which is conventionally assumed to be medium independent. We promote this assumption to a dynamical question by making the model scale invariant using a dilaton compensator $χ$, so that the effective chiral invariant mass $m_{\rm inv}^\ast = m_0\tildeχ$, with $\tildeχ= χ/f_χ$, responds to the partial restoration of scale symmetry in the medium. We fit the model parameters by using vacuum spectra, nuclear matter properties, and NICER mass--radius posteriors---with the hadronic equation of state connected to 2+1-flavor Nambu--Jona-Lasinio quark matter by an interpolation. The best fit gives $m_0 = 657$ MeV, a maximum neutron-star mass of $2.30\,M_\odot$ and $R_{1.4} = 12.22$ km, with the mass--radius sequence passing through all three NICER credible regions. The resulting tidal deformabilities, $Λ_{1.4} = 387$ and $\tildeΛ= 463$, are consistent with GW170817 measurements. The in-medium analysis separates the two restorations: at the hadron--quark matching density the chiral condensate falls to $56\%$ of its vacuum value, while the dilaton decreases only to $94\%$, so the nucleon arrives at the matching density with $90\%$ of its mass carried by the invariant part. The order parameters of chiral and scale symmetries organize the in-medium probes, making the $ω$ an almost pure probe of scale symmetry and the $ρ$ of chiral restoration, which gives us a clue on the origin of hadron mass.

title: Correlations and fluctuations of flow with event shape engineering in Pb-Pb and Xe-Xe collisions at the LHC
comment: 28 pages, 15 captioned figures, authors from page 23, submitted to PLB, figures at http://alice-publications.web.cern.ch/node/13698
summary: Measurements of anisotropic flow provide some of the strongest constraints on the collective expansion and transport properties of the quark-gluon plasma produced in ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions. In this paper, correlations and fluctuations of the anisotropic flow coefficients $v_{2}$, $v_{3}$, and $v_{4}$ are measured in Pb-Pb and Xe-Xe collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm{NN}}} = 5.02$ and $5.44$ TeV, respectively, with the ALICE detector. The Event Shape Engineering technique, based on the reduced flow vector $q_{n}$, is used to study flow correlations for different initial-state geometries. A strong anticorrelation between $v_2$ and $v_3$ and a positive correlation between $v_2$ and $v_4$ are observed. A small anticorrelation is seen between $v_3$ and $v_4$. From the $v_2$-$v_4$ correlation, the linear and nonlinear components of $v_4$ are extracted and compared to those extracted using multiparticle correlations. The linear and nonlinear components of $v_{4}$ are also measured directly as a function of $q_2$ for the first time in Pb-Pb and Xe-Xe, revealing a strong coupling of the nonlinear term to the initial-state ellipticity $\varepsilon_2$, while the linear component shows little dependence on initial-state geometry. Additionally, the coupling coefficient $χ_{4,22}$, which measures the nonlinear contribution of $v_2^2$ to $v_4$, is extracted and shows little dependence on $q_2$, except in very central collisions. The effects of flow fluctuations for constrained initial-state geometries are studied for the first time using Event Shape Engineering with the ratio of $v_2\{2\}$ and $v_2\{4\}$; the results show that collisions with the lowest $q_2$ exhibit more significant $v_2$ fluctuations compared to the unbiased ratio.

title: Constrained Hamiltonian Formulation of Kinetic Theory for Relativistic Spin-$1/2$ Particles
summary: Describing spin transport away from equilibrium requires a kinetic theory that consistently incorporates spin dynamics and phase space structure. We construct such a collisionless kinetic theory for relativistic spin-$1/2$ particles in external electromagnetic fields using the constrained Hamiltonian formalism. The formulation yields both a covariant kinetic equation and its form in independent physical phase space variables, together with the associated noncanonical Poisson brackets and invariant measure. For massive particles, the interplay between the spin constraints and the electromagnetic field makes the particle velocity generally nonparallel to its kinetic momentum and modifies the momentum and spin evolution. The invariant measure in the reduced phase space obeys an exact Liouville identity even for time-dependent fields. This identity and the equations of motion give local conservation of charge and Boltzmann entropy, as well as balance equations for energy-momentum and total angular momentum. The global equilibrium conditions are consistent with covariant statistical mechanics and the Wigner function approach. The massless construction recovers the standard chiral kinetic equations and phase space measure. This framework provides a consistent Hamiltonian description of spin transport beyond equilibrium.

comment: 5 pages, 2 figures, plus 2 pages End Matter with 2 figures and 2 tables

title: Hypersurface covariance in relativistic local equilibrium
summary: Defining equilibrium typically requires specifying a three-dimensional spacelike hypersurface. While global equilibrium is hypersurface covariant, calculations involving local equilibrium can exhibit hypersurface dependence. In this work, we use polarization in heavy-ion collisions within the Zubarev response approach as an example to show that the hypersurface dependence arising from the local-equilibrium part of the density operator is canceled by an overlooked nondissipative contribution from its so-called ``dissipative part". We establish a hypersurface-covariant Zubarev framework for general geometries by consistently including both nondissipative and dissipative parts, eliminating dependence on the arbitrary hypersurface vector. The remaining frame dependence is physical: it arises from the medium rest frame entering the particle distribution and the time direction of the dissipative process, which usually coincide. This resolves, in principle, the longstanding and widely discussed conceptual disagreement over hypersurface dependence between two influential studies addressing the sign puzzles of $Λ$-hyperon polarization in heavy-ion collisions
